title: Collaborator Guide — Contribute to a Proposal

hero.h1: Contribute to a Proposal, Scoped to You
lede: You were invited to help on one proposal. This guide is your complete manual: accept the invite, find your assigned sections, contribute in the canvas, comment, move files, and understand exactly what each grant unlocks.
Collaborators are stage-scoped — you see exactly what you were invited to, and nothing else.
hero.badge: Scoped access · every control your grant unlocks, and every boundary

footer: govwin — RFP Pipeline Portal · Collaborator role. Your access is granted per proposal by that company’s admin and can be adjusted or revoked at any time. Companion guides: Customer-Admin, RFP-Admin Operations.

sections.heading: Orientation — a scoped collaborator
sections.lead: You’ve been invited to help on one proposal at one company. This guide is your whole world in the platform: what you can open, how you contribute, and where your assignments live. Collaborators are stage-scoped — your access is granted per section and per permission (view, comment, or edit).
sections.caption: The collaborator landing — scoped to the work you were invited to.

callouts.html: There are two kinds of invite. An External invite makes you a partner_user — the scoped collaborator this guide covers. A Contributor invite makes you internal staff (tenant-wide). If you see the full company sidebar, you were invited as a Contributor; if you see only Proposals, you’re an External collaborator.

sections.heading: Accept your invite & sign in
sections.lead: Your invite arrives as a deep-linked email from the company that wants your help.

steps.t: Follow the email link to /invite/<token>. The Accept Invitation page names the inviter, the proposal, the company, and your email.
Set a Password (at least 12 characters) and Confirm Password, then Set Password & Accept. You’re dropped straight into the proposal workspace.
If you’re an existing user, you’re auto-accepted and the email links you straight to the proposal — no password step.

callouts.html: A revoked invite shows “This invitation is no longer valid.” An already-used one shows Invite Already Accepted with a Go to Login button. First sign-in on a fresh account asks you to change your temporary password before anything else.

sections.heading: Your landing — only your assigned work
sections.lead: Unlike a customer admin, your home is the proposals list scoped to you. The sidebar shows only Proposals (plus the notification bell and Sign out) — no dashboard, pipeline, library, or billing.
sections.caption: The scoped landing — the proposals you’re invited to, and only those.

steps.t: Open the proposal you were invited to. Inside, the workspace defaults to the My Sections tab — the sections assigned to you, each with a permission pill (edit / comment / view).
If nothing’s assigned yet, you’ll see “No sections are assigned to you yet.” until an admin adds you.

callouts.html: Navigating to a company screen you’re not scoped for (dashboard, library, buckets, billing) simply redirects you back to Proposals. Nothing breaks — you’re gently kept in your lane.

sections.heading: Inside the proposal — your view
sections.lead: The proposal workspace, scoped to you, is organized into what you can act on.
sections.caption: Inside a proposal — your assignments, dropbox, and the activity timeline.
sections.body: The Contributor View groups your work: My Assignments (or Shared With Me for externals) — the sections you can edit, each with a status badge, page progress, and Open Editor →; My Dropbox — your private file drop for this proposal; Add content — offer a document into the company library; Sections (Comment Only) with View & Comment; and Other Sections (View Only) with View. A Timeline tab shows the proposal’s activity feed.

steps.t: Open a section you can edit and work in the same canvas editor the customer uses — headings, text, lists, tables, images as structured nodes.
steps.cap: The canvas editor — your contribution surface (per your edit grant).

steps.t: Your edits save to the shared draft. The section owner reviews and, when it’s right, Accepts & Locks it — that’s an admin action; your job is to get the content right and save.

callouts.html: If the agency amends the solicitation, an amber banner appears at the top of the workspace with the change. You can read it (and expand the compliance delta), but only a company admin can acknowledge it — “An admin must acknowledge these changes.” Re-check any section you’re drafting against the change.

sections.heading: Your permission matrix
sections.lead: Everything you can do flows from your grant on a section. Here is exactly what each level unlocks — this is the single most useful reference in this guide.

table.title: What view / comment / edit unlock
rows: Accept & Lock · advance stage · manage team

callouts.html: * A view collaborator can resolve a comment on a section they can see, but their comment posts are rejected. Accepting/locking, advancing stages, and exporting the whole proposal are always admin-only — a collaborator’s contribution ends at Save + comment.

sections.heading: Comment & suggest
sections.lead: Comments are how you contribute without changing the draft directly. They thread per section (surfaced in the Node tab when a node is selected, and in the dedicated Review tab).

steps.t: Type in Add comment… and press Enter or click Add. A “reply” is simply another comment on the same section thread.
Click Resolve (on a human comment) or Dismiss (on an 🤖 AI Review item). Resolved comments collapse under a Show/Hide N resolved toggle.

callouts.html: Resolving is one-way (there’s no un-resolve), and comments can’t be edited or deleted — so post a fresh comment to add or correct something.

sections.heading: Files — dropbox & add content
sections.where: section workspace → My Dropbox · Add content
sections.body: My Dropbox is your private per-proposal file drop — you see only your own files (delete your own with the ×). Add content lets you offer a document into the company library: drop a file and it’s atomized (“Atomized N files into M atoms. Review in Library.”). The upload works even though the Library link itself is out of your scope — an admin reviews what you contributed.

callouts.html: Uploads are blocked once the proposal is locked (you’ll get a clear message). Before the first lock, section export is also unavailable (“Downloads available after final review and lock”).

sections.heading: Collaboration vaults (“nooks”) — your shared workspace
sections.lead: A collaboration vault (a “nook”) is a shared library a company opens with one outside partner. You reach it from Collaboration vaults in your sidebar — and you see it only once somebody adds you to one. Until then the link takes you back to your proposals, which is the product telling you there is nothing of yours there yet, not an error.

steps.t: Sign in. If your only access is a nook, you land on /vaults — a simple list of the customer(s) you collaborate with. Click Open nook → to enter.
steps.cap: Your /vaults list — only the customer(s) you collaborate with.

steps.t: Add an artifact — name it, pick its form (Document · Deck · Sheet · PDF), and add it. Your upload is atomized into the nook (it is invisible to the customer’s main library until they choose to harvest it).
Download a whole artifact in any format (.docx · .pptx · .xlsx · .pdf). You can download whole artifacts only — pulling out individual sections is a customer-side action.

table.title: What you can do in a nook
rows: Harvest content into the proposal library
Invite / remove members, close the nook

callouts.html: When you add content, the customer is notified and a review task is raised on their side — they decide what (if anything) to pull into their proposal. Only add content you’re comfortable with the customer using.
A nook is deliberately quiet: no main-library clutter, no other partners. Everything you add stays scoped to that one customer relationship.

Not illustrated on purpose. A vault only renders for a collaborator who is a member of one, and the capture that produced this guide refused to photograph the redirect rather than show you a picture of the proposals list captioned as a vault.

sections.heading: Scope boundaries — what’s out of reach
sections.lead: By design, a collaborator can’t see the company’s book of business. This keeps their pipeline, library, and billing private while still letting you do the work you were brought in for.

table.title: Where the boundaries are
rows: Dashboard · Opportunities · Buckets · Library · Builds · Processes · Activity · Team · Documents · Settings
not found — you can’t even open it by URL
An edit on a comment/view section
rejected server-side (403) even if you forge the request

callouts.html: Access is a living grant. An admin can widen it (view → comment → edit), narrow it, or revoke it. If your access ends, your collaborator membership at that company is cleanly removed — without touching any other company you collaborate with. Re-inviting a revoked email restores the same record with fresh grants.

sections.heading: Your lifecycle & states
sections.lead: A quick reference for where you stand at any moment.

table.title: Collaborator states
rows: invite sent, not yet accepted — the /invite link is live until used or revoked
accepted but nothing assigned yet — “No sections are assigned to you yet.”
only your assigned sections at your granted permission, plus dropbox & add-content
the review/locked banner; saving & uploading pause; export of your sections opens after the first lock
access ends immediately; the invite link reads “no longer valid.” Re-invite restores it

callouts.html: Your contribution is real work the team depends on — draft and comment your assigned sections, keep your dropbox current, and the admin carries it across the finish line by accepting and locking.

There is no company-wide activity feed for you. /activity belongs to the company’s own staff; asking for it returns you to your proposals. What you did is recorded — it appears in the company’s audit trail and on the sections you touched — you simply do not hold the company-wide view.
